items.stem: An agent change in Spring Boot altered transaction boundaries. What is the right response?

options.text: Reject the change, re-scope the task and review the corrected diff
options.rationale: Correct: transaction-affecting changes must be reviewed and re-scoped.

options.text: Merge it since the application still starts
options.rationale: Starting is not evidence that transactions are correct.

options.text: Disable transactions to avoid the problem
Let the agent keep editing until tests pass
options.rationale: Blind iteration can mask the real defect.

items.explanation: Correct: transaction-affecting changes must be reviewed and re-scoped.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO steps make AI-generated Spring Boot components trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Check bean wiring, scope and configuration after generation
options.rationale: Correct: generated wiring can be subtly wrong and must be verified.

options.text: Run and read the tests that exercise the component
options.rationale: Correct: executing tests confirms behaviour, not just compilation.

options.text: Assume injection is correct because it compiles
options.rationale: Compilation does not prove correct runtime wiring.

options.text: Paste the production datasource password for context
options.rationale: Secrets must never go into prompts.

items.explanation: Correct: generated wiring can be subtly wrong and must be verified.

items.stem: Where should datasource passwords live when working in Cursor?

options.text: In externalised configuration or a secret store, never in a prompt
options.rationale: Correct: credentials stay in configuration and out of prompts.

options.text: Pasted into the chat so the agent has full context
options.rationale: Prompts should never carry live credentials.

options.text: Hard-coded in the application properties committed to git
options.rationale: Committed secrets leak and cannot be rotated safely.

options.text: In a code comment for convenience
options.rationale: Comments are committed source and expose the secret.

items.explanation: Correct: credentials stay in configuration and out of prompts.
